rationale: Per-channel learnable alpha vector (shape (1,c,1,1), all init 0.1) replacing the scalar per-block alpha from iter-14. Tests channel-wise modulation of the EDSR residual scaling mechanism. Param cost negligible: 12 scalars -> 384 entries, total 0.2247M -> 0.2251M.
advice_for_others: Discard. val_ssim 0.6630 -> 0.6454 (-2.7%), headroom 0.5870 -> 0.5656 (-2.14pp). Channel-wise alpha modulation hurts despite identical init. Diagnosis: at c=32 / 6 blocks / 8 epochs / 400 phantoms, per-channel alpha lets individual channels drift away from the 0.1 sweet spot during training (the 384 scalars all start equal but have no constraint to remain co-scaled), polluting the signal. Combined with iter-15 (-4.9pp at alpha=0.05) and iter-17 (-4.6pp at alpha=0.2), the conclusion is firm: the alpha-shape/init axis is closed — exactly 0.1 scalar per block is the local optimum. ALPHA-GATING AXIS NOW COMPLETELY CLOSED at this data/depth budget. Next directions to try: kernel-3->5 (iter-28, untested spatial-mixing axis), i0 noise jitter (iter-30), or larger structural swings (NAFNet cross-port).
